test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the reference of the Delhi Sultanate, what was the 'Group of Forty'?

options.text: They were mostly powerful Turkish slaves of Iltutmish, who took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziyya's killing.
They were forty military archers who distinguished themselves by their bravery in the Delhi Sultanate.
They were forty banjara leaders who transferred military supplies in times of war.
They were forty Rajput nobles who planned a coup to dethrone Qutb ud Din Aibak in 1210.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Group of Forty' or 'Chihalgani'** was a significant political faction in the **Delhi Sultanate during the 13th century. **
 
• This group was **primarily composed of forty powerful Turkish nobles** and slaves who were closely associated with Sultan Iltutmish (reigned 1211-1236)
 
• This group was responsible for** various critical roles in the military, administration, and governance.**
 
• After **the death of Iltutmish in 1236,** the Chihalgani became very powerful, exerting substantial influence over the succession and governance of the Sultanate. 
 
• Iltutmish, daughter Raziyya Sultan ascended to the throne but her reign faced strong opposition, particularly from the Chihalgani

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iltutmish (Reigned 1211-1236)**

 
 
• Iltutmish was originally a **slave of Qutb-ud-din Aibak,** the founder of the Mamluk Dynasty.
 
• He became **Sultan of Delhi after defeating Aram Shah,** a rival claimant, thereby solidifying his position as the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish is **credited with consolidating and centralizing the administration of the Delhi Sultanate,** setting up an efficient governance structure.
 
• He** introduced the iqta system**, where land was granted to military commanders in exchange for their services.
 
 
 
• **Razia Sultan (Reigned 1236-1240)**
 
 
• **​**Razia Sultan was **the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate**, breaking significant gender barriers in the Muslim world.
 
• **Nominated by her father Iltutmish**, she overcame initial resistance from the nobility to ascend to the throne.
 
• Razia was **known for her competent administration**, showing a commitment to justice and effective governance.
